# Depths

> Generates a six-level elevation scale of layered box-shadows — a tight key
> shadow, a soft ambient, an optional contact layer — from one light source and
> three curves, mapped to semantic tokens like `shadow-raised` and
> `shadow-modal`. Honest about dark mode, and a handoff written for a coding
> agent.

Free, no account, no API key, no rate limit. Every scale is a pure function of
the URL, so the same link always returns the same shadows.

## Why this exists

Color has ramps and tokens. Motion has curves and durations. Shadows are still
five `box-shadow` strings someone copied from five different places, at five
inconsistent angles, with no rule about which surface gets which. An agent
asked to "add a shadow to the dropdown" has nothing to reach for. This produces
a scale where every level is derived from one light source, every token names a
surface, and the dark-mode values state their own limits.

## Using this as a tool

Build a URL and fetch it. **You do not need to run JavaScript** — the server
injects the whole scale into the HTML as both a `<pre>` block and a
`<script type="application/json">`, so a plain fetch of any URL below returns
readable data. (Both shapes on purpose: HTML-to-markdown conversion strips
script tags, so JSON alone would be invisible to the tools most likely to be
reading this.)

If you want data without the page around it, `/api/shadows` takes the same
query string:

- `https://www.depths.studio/api/shadows` — the default scale, as JSON
- `https://www.depths.studio/api/shadows?format=text` — the same, as plain text
- `https://www.depths.studio/api/shadows?p=crisp&a=120` — a different scale

The JSON carries a `version` key, currently `1`. Keys are only ever added, and
the meaning of an existing key never changes within a version — treat a
`version` you do not know as a reason to stop rather than to guess.

The page itself takes the same parameters:

- `https://www.depths.studio/` — the default scale
- `https://www.depths.studio/?p=dramatic` — a different preset
- `https://www.depths.studio/?a=135&c=1e2a4a` — upper-left light, tinted ink

### Parameters

All values are plain decimals — no scaling tables, no base64. Anything out of
range is clamped rather than rejected, an unparseable field is dropped with a
note on the page (and a `warnings` key in the JSON), and a link always resolves
to a renderable scale.

| Param | Required | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `p` | no | `soft` (default), `crisp`, `dramatic`, `hairline` | The preset — a bundle of the five curve values below. |
| `a` | no | 0–360 | Light angle in degrees, standard math convention: 90 (default) is overhead, 45 is upper-right, 135 is upper-left. Shadows fall away from the light. Wraps rather than clamps. |
| `d` | no | 0.25–8 | Distance: the key shadow's offset in px at level 1. The scale's base unit. |
| `g` | no | 1.1–3 | Growth: per-level multiplier on the offset. `g=1.9` means each level throws ~2x further than the last. |
| `b` | no | 0.5–6 | Blur, as a multiple of the offset. Low is crisp, high is diffuse. |
| `o` | no | 1–40 | Opacity: the key layer's alpha at level 1, in percent. |
| `f` | no | 0.6–1.2 | Falloff: per-level multiplier on opacity. Below 1, higher levels are more transparent. |
| `y` | no | `2` or `3` | Layers per level: key + ambient, or with a contact shadow added. |
| `c` | no | 6 hex digits, no `#` | Tinted shadow ink. Omit for black. |
| `k` | no | `s` or `sb` (default) | Dark strategy: boosted shadows alone, or shadows plus hairline `--edge-*` borders. |
| `pu` | no | e.g. `modal5.hover3` | Move tokens to other levels: token short-name then level digit, dot-joined. `none` and `pressed` cannot move. |
| `xt` | no | e.g. `pressed.toast` | Exclude tokens from export, dot-separated short names. Filters output only — the scale still resolves in full. |

Curve values omitted from the URL take the chosen preset's values, so a bare
link is a preset and a parameterized one names exactly its differences.

## The tokens

Short name is what `pu` and `xt` use; the exported variable is `--shadow-<name>`.

| Token | Level | Use when | Not when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | 0 | Inputs, list rows, tables — anything that belongs to the page rather than sitting on it. | Don't use elevation to fix a contrast problem; that's a color decision. |
| `raised` | 1 | The default for anything that reads as an object: cards, tiles, buttons. | Not for nesting — a raised card inside a raised card flattens both. |
| `hover` | 2 | On hover or focus of an element that is `raised` at rest, so the lift reads as one step up. | Not as a resting state — if everything is lifted, nothing is. |
| `sticky` | 2 | Bars that pin over scrolling content, once content actually passes beneath them. | Not while the page sits at the top — a shadow over nothing announces machinery. |
| `dropdown` | 3 | Transient surfaces summoned from a control: menus, popovers, tooltips. | Not for dialogs that take over the page — that is `modal`'s job. |
| `modal` | 4 | Surfaces that block the page behind a scrim and hold focus. | Not for toasts — a modal shadow on a toast makes a notification feel like an interruption. |
| `toast` | 5 | The top of the stack: transient messages floating over everything. | Never on persistent chrome. The top level is loud because nothing lives there. |
| `pressed` | inset | Wells, active toggle tracks, pressed states — surfaces pushed below the page. | Not for disabled states; depressed and disabled are different messages. |

## Rules the scale is built on

Worth knowing if you are going to wire these into a product.

- **One light source.** Every level's offsets point the same way, derived from
  `a`. Mixed shadow angles are the most common tell of an unsystematized UI.
- **Levels are a geometric progression.** Offset and blur grow by `g` per
  level, so the scale reads as one material photographed at different heights,
  not eight unrelated shadows.
- **One step per interaction.** Hover moves an element exactly one token —
  raised to hover — never two.
- **Don't nest elevation.** The inner surface of a raised card goes back to
  `shadow-none`.
- **Dark mode is honest, not equivalent.** Alphas are boosted x1.5 (capped at
  0.85) and hairline `--edge-*` borders are added, but elevation on a dark page
  is mostly carried by surface color. Pair these tokens with a lightened
  surface ramp — https://www.ramps.studio/ generates one — and let the shadow
  support it.
- **`pressed` is an inset, outside the scale.** It derives from the base unit,
  not the growth curve: a well does not get deeper when a dropdown gets higher.
- **Never animate between distant levels.** Raised to hover is designed for;
  none to modal reads as a glitch — fade the surface in at its final elevation.

## Exports

Everything is generated client-side; the endpoints recompute the same pure
function server-side for readers without JavaScript.

- **CSS** — custom properties, light in `:root`, boosted dark values under
  `.dark`, plus `--edge-*` hairlines that are transparent in light mode so they
  can ship unconditionally without shifting layout.
- **Tailwind** — a v4 `@theme` block. The theme points at intermediate
  variables that `.dark` redefines, because `@theme` values are inlined into
  the generated utilities and a plain dark override would change nothing.
- **JSON (DTCG)** — the W3C composite `shadow` type, for Style Dictionary and
  similar pipelines. Dark values ride in `$extensions["studio.depths"]`; there
  is deliberately no Figma export, because Figma variables have no shadow type.
- **Native (SwiftUI)** — an enum of the tokens plus a colorScheme-aware
  `.depthsShadow(_:)` modifier that chains the layers. CSS blur converts to
  SwiftUI radius at blur / 2 (stated in the file's own header); the pressed
  inset uses `ShapeStyle.shadow(.inner)`, iOS 16 / macOS 13 and up.
- **Markdown** — the token table, the CSS, and the rules above, written to be
  pasted into an agent's context.

## Other tools in this family

Same contract everywhere: state lives in the query string, every page serves
its values as plain text without JavaScript, and there is no account, key or
rate limit. Generated from the shared manifest — see `src/shared/tools.ts`.

  Springs  Motion, easings & durations     https://www.springs.studio/
  Beeps    UI sounds & feedback            https://www.beeps.studio/
  Texts    Type styles & scaling           not yet released
  SVGs     Icon cleanup & alignment        not yet released
